READ-ONLY: no commits, pushes, or edits. Verify the fix for your NEW-1 blocker in 'git diff main' at /home/luandro/.local/share/opencode/worktree/0ede94/free-models-junior (head e22f6eb).

NEW-1 was: refresh.sh used plain 'ln -T' which fails when the destination exists, so every scheduled refresh discarded its output and the catalogue froze; install.sh had the same shape on --update.

Claimed fix: refresh.sh uses 'ln -T -f' for catalogue and state, guarded by ownership + unchanged-content checks above each call. install.sh's publish_no_clobber takes a replace arg, 1 only when --update verified ownership and unchanged content; first install still uses plain 'ln -T'. Bootstrap skips the filter when --update finds an owned unchanged catalogue.

Focus: with -f now in use, can either script overwrite a file it does NOT own? Trace every call site and the checks that guard it. Also confirm the author's empirical result that generated_unix now advances across a wrapper run.

Output BLOCKER/RISK/NIT/OK with file:line. Be concise.
